neighbours.label: The 'phe'/'fe' piece of the name Orpheus in any spelling and any use, myth or not (Orpheus, Orfeo, Orphée, Orfeón, the Orpheum theatre, a boat named Orpheo); weaker for Morpheus and Orphic. Quiet for the Orpheus story told without the name (Eurydice, the lyre player who looked back), for orphan/orphanage, and for other Greek heroes (Theseus, Perseus). Also fires on the closing '*' of a wide space-padded comment-box line in code.
fire: A brass band called Orfeón Donostiarra toured Spain.
Orpheus charmed the rocks and trees with his music.
Monteverdi's opera L'Orfeo premiered in Mantua in 1607.
Cocteau's film Orphée moves the myth to postwar Paris.
We saw a vaudeville revival at the old Orpheum theatre downtown.
The fishing boat Orpheo was tied up at the end of the pier.
The choir Orfeón Catalán sang at the festival last spring.
quiet: The poet with the lyre charmed the rocks and trees with his music.
Monteverdi's opera about a grieving singer premiered in Mantua in 1607.
Eurydice was lost forever when the musician looked back at the gate.
We saw a vaudeville revival at the old Palace theatre downtown.
The fishing boat Neptune was tied up at the end of the pier.
The children's orphanage held a concert at the festival last spring.
Theseus found his way out of the labyrinth with a thread.
Perseus cut off the head of Medusa with a polished shield.
